title: Email
content:
# Email Read and search Outlook mail, send, reply and forward, schedule and track sends, work with drafts, categories, send-as addresses and signatures, and catch bounces. Every call takes the `accountId` of a Microsoft account connected with `scopes=email`. Ids are Microsoft Graph message and folder ids, a thread id is Outlook's conversation id, and every object carries `provider` and `accountId`. ## List and search threads `GET /v1/email/threads` returns threads newest first, from the inbox unless you pass `folder`: ```bash curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/threads?accountId=ACCOUNT_ID&folder=inbox&unread=true&limit=20" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" ``` ```json { "data": [ { "id": "AAQkAGI2…", "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "provider": "microsoft", "subject": "Contract for Q4", "snippet": "Hi Ana, attached is the signed version…", "unread": true, "latestMessageReceivedAt": "2026-10-26T09:12:00.000Z" } ], "pagination": { "hasMore": true, "nextCursor": "…" }, "meta": { "filteredClientSide": [] } } ``` `GET /v1/email/messages` takes the same filters and returns single messages. Both page with `cursor` and `limit` (up to 200, default 50). ## Filter and search | Parameter | What it does | |-----------|--------------| | `folder` | `inbox`, `sent`, `drafts`, `trash` (Deleted Items), `spam` (Junk Email), `archive`, or a folder id from `GET /v1/email/folders` | | `unread`, `starred`, `hasAttachment` | `true` or `false` | | `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `anyEmail` | An address. `anyEmail` matches any participant | | `subject` | Words in the subject | | `after`, `before` | ISO 8601 bounds on the message date | | `searchQueryNative` | A Microsoft Graph `$search` query passed as it is, such as `subject:invoice` (up to 500 characters) | | `sortOrder` | `desc` (default) or `asc` | Outlook cannot combine a search with other filters, so with `searchQueryNative` the other filters run on the fetched page. `bcc` and `anyEmail` always do. A filter Outlook cannot apply itself is applied to the fetched page and named in `meta.filteredClientSide`. Such a page can hold fewer than `limit` items while `pagination.hasMore` stays `true`. ## Read a thread or message `GET /v1/email/threads/{threadId}?accountId=…` returns the thread with its messages. `GET /v1/email/messages/{messageId}?accountId=…` returns one message with `text`, `html` and `attachments`. Add `includeHeaders=true` for the headers, or `raw=true` for the full MIME source. Add `clean=true` to either call for a `clean` object on each message, ready to hand to an LLM: ```json "clean": { "text": "Sounds good, Thursday at 3 works.\n\nAna Ruiz\nHead of Ops, Acme", "status": "stripped", "removed": { "quoted": true, "forwardHeader": false, "boilerplate": true }, "signature": "Ana Ruiz\nHead of Ops, Acme", "forwarded": null } ``` `text` drops quoted replies, tracking pixels and footers such as "Sent from my iPhone", in the common languages. The signature stays in `text` and also comes alone in `signature`. A forward keeps the forwarded content, and its From, To, Date and Subject come parsed in `forwarded`. `text` is never empty for a mail with a body: when nothing can be stripped safely you get the whole body with `status: "fallback"`. The rules are deterministic; no model reads the mail. ## Send an email `POST /v1/email/messages` sends from the connected mailbox and returns the sent copy with `201`: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/messages" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "to": [{ "email": "client@example.com", "name": "Client" }], "subject": "Your booking", "html": "

See you on Tuesday.

", "attachments": [{ "filename": "invoice.pdf", "contentType": "application/pdf", "url": "https://example.com/invoice.pdf" }], "metadata": { "bookingId": "bk_123" } }' ``` | Field | What it does | |-------|--------------| | `to`, `cc`, `bcc` | Up to 100 addresses each, as `{ email, name? }`. `to` needs at least one | | `replyTo` | Up to 5 addresses | | `subject` | Up to 998 characters | | `text`, `html` | At least one | | `attachments` | Up to 20 and 25 MB in total, as `{ filename, contentType, url }` or `{ filename, contentType, base64 }`. Add `contentId` to reference an inline image from `html` | | `replyToMessageId` | Threads the email under that message | | `headers` | Custom headers. Only names starting with `X-` are accepted. `List-Unsubscribe` headers are dropped and named in the returned `metadata.droppedHeaders` | | `metadata` | String pairs echoed on the returned message | ## Schedule a send Add `scheduledFor` to a send or a reply, as ISO 8601 between 1 minute and 30 days ahead. Zernio answers `202` with the scheduled send and sends it within a minute of that time: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/messages" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "to": [{ "email": "client@example.com" }], "subject": "Following up", "html": "

Any questions about the proposal?

", "scheduledFor": "2026-11-12T09:00:00Z" }' ``` ```json { "data": { "id": "SCHEDULE_ID", "status": "scheduled", "scheduledFor": "2026-11-12T09:00:00.000Z", "to": [{ "email": "client@example.com" }], "subject": "Following up" } } ``` - `GET /v1/email/messages/scheduled?accountId=…` lists scheduled sends in send order. Filter with `status`: `scheduled`, `sending`, `sent`, `failed` or `cancelled`. - `GET /v1/email/messages/scheduled/{scheduleId}?accountId=…` reads one. Once sent it carries `sentMessageId` and `sentThreadId`. - `DELETE /v1/email/messages/scheduled/{scheduleId}?accountId=…` cancels one that has not left yet. Later it answers `409`. The account and its areas are checked when you schedule. The daily cap and cooldowns apply when the email leaves. If it cannot leave then, it moves to `failed` with an `error` and Zernio fires `email.send_failed`. Nothing is retried, so schedule it again once the cause is fixed. ### Hold it as a draft in the mailbox Add `"holdAsDraft": true` next to `scheduledFor` to save the email as a draft in Outlook right away. The user can read and edit it there, and Zernio sends the draft as it stands at `scheduledFor`. The scheduled send then carries `holdAsDraft: true` and `draftId`, the Outlook message id. Cancelling it deletes the draft. If the draft is deleted or sent from the mailbox first, the send moves to `failed` and Zernio fires `email.send_failed`. `holdAsDraft` without `scheduledFor` answers `400`. ## Track opens, clicks and replies Add any of these to a send or a reply: | Field | What it does | Webhook | |-------|--------------|---------| | `trackOpens` | Adds a 1x1 image to the `html` | `email.opened` | | `trackLinks` | Sends every `http(s)` link in the `html` through a Zernio redirect to the original URL | `email.link_clicked` | | `trackReplies` | Watches the Outlook conversation for mail from anyone other than the mailbox | `email.thread_replied` | The sent message carries a `trackingId`, and every tracking webhook carries it with the message's `messageId`, `threadId` and your `metadata`. `trackOpens` and `trackLinks` need `html`. `trackReplies` works with `text` too. Tracking is free. Opens are a signal, not proof of reading: - Image proxies such as Gmail's and Apple Mail's fetch the pixel themselves, some as soon as the mail arrives. - Clients that block images never report an open. - Opening the message in the mailbox's own Sent folder counts. Mail security gateways sometimes follow links on delivery, which reports a click. Auto-replies count as replies. A bounce does not: it fires `email.bounced`. ## Reply to a message `POST /v1/email/messages/{messageId}/reply` replies inside the Outlook conversation. Outlook adds the quoted original below your `text` or `html`. It goes to the original sender, or with `mode: "replyAll"` to every recipient too: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/messages/MESSAGE_ID/reply" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "mode": "replyAll", "text": "Thanks, confirmed." }' ``` `to` and `subject` are optional on a reply and default to the original's. Replies count against the same daily cap as sends. ## Forward a message `POST /v1/email/messages/{messageId}/forward` forwards the mail with its attachments. Your `text` or `html` goes above it, and the subject defaults to `Fwd:` plus the original's: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/messages/MESSAGE_ID/forward" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: 3f1c9a2e-forward-1" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "to": [{ "email": "sales@acme.com" }], "text": "Can you take this one?", "excludeAttachmentIds": ["ATTACHMENT_ID"] }' ``` It goes through Outlook's own forward, so Outlook writes the forward header. Tracking, `from` and the send caps work as on a send, and the response carries `forwardedFrom`. `includeAttachments: false` keeps only the original's inline images. `excludeAttachmentIds` leaves out the attachments you name, by the ids a read of the message returned. Everything together stays under 25 MB, else `413 attachment_too_large`. ## Work with drafts Drafts suit an agent that writes and a person who approves. `POST /v1/email/drafts` saves a draft in the mailbox, where the user sees it in Outlook. Recipients and subject can wait. `inReplyTo` makes a reply draft in that thread, and `forwardOf` a forward draft with the original's attachments: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/drafts" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "inReplyTo": "MESSAGE_ID", "html": "

Proposed answer

" }' ``` The draft comes back with its `id`, a `kind` (`new`, `reply` or `forward`, fixed for its life) and a `version`. Store the `id`; `messageId` changes on every save. | Call | What it does | |------|--------------| | `GET /v1/email/drafts` | Lists the mailbox's drafts, the user's own included | | `GET /v1/email/drafts/{draftId}` | Reads a draft as it stands now | | `PATCH /v1/email/drafts/{draftId}` | Changes the fields you send and keeps the rest | | `DELETE /v1/email/drafts/{draftId}` | Deletes it | | `POST /v1/email/drafts/{draftId}/send` | Sends it, with any edits the user made in Outlook | ### Approve exactly one version The `version` changes whenever anyone edits the draft, the user in Outlook included. Pass it as `If-Match` on `PATCH` or send. If the draft changed since, you get `412 draft_conflict` with the current draft in `details.draft`, so you can review what the person wrote: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/drafts/DRAFT_ID/send" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "If-Match: \"VERSION\"" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID" }' ``` The sent message carries `draftId`, and `email.sent` fires with `source: "draft"`. A second send while one is in flight answers `409 draft_sending`, and a draft the user deleted or sent answers `404 draft_not_found`. Add `sendAt` to send later instead: you get `202` with a scheduled send, and the draft stays editable until then. Cancelling it keeps the draft. Tracking set at creation applies. If an edit removed the open pixel or tracked links, Zernio puts them back before sending. ## Detect bounces When a recipient's server refuses a mail, the bounce report lands in the mailbox and Zernio fires `email.bounced`, once per failed recipient. Delay warnings and out-of-office replies do not fire it. Act on `bounce.recommendedAction`: | `recommendedAction` | When | What to do | |---------------------|------|------------| | `remove` | `user_unknown`, `domain_not_found` | Stop sending to this address | | `retry` | `mailbox_full`, `rate_limited`, any soft bounce | Try again later | | `fix_configuration` | `auth_failure`, `blocklisted` | Fix SPF, DKIM, DMARC or your sending reputation | | `review` | `spam_blocked`, `policy_blocked`, `message_too_large`, `content_rejected`, `other` | Look at the content or the recipient's policy | The event also carries `type` (`hard`, `soft` or `undetermined`), the `status` such as `5.1.1`, a numeric `smtpCode`, the server's `diagnostic`, and `detection`. Bounces arrive minutes to days after the send; `bouncedAt` and `detectedAt` show both times. When the send had tracking, `email.messageId`, `trackingId` and `metadata` are set. Otherwise match on `threadId`, `internetMessageId` or the quoted `subject`. ## Send from another address `GET /v1/email/send-as?accountId=…` lists the mailbox address and its aliases. Microsoft Graph cannot list shared mailboxes or delegated rights, so declare those once: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/send-as" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "email": "support@contoso.com", "name": "Contoso Support" }' ``` Then pass it as `from` on a send, reply or scheduled send. A `from` that is neither listed nor declared answers `400`. Exchange decides at send time. Without Send As or Send on Behalf rights on the address, the send answers `403`; an Exchange admin grants the right. A declared address turns `accepted` after its first send. When the mailbox only has Send on Behalf, the sent message shows the mailbox in `sender` and the shared address in `from`. ### Signatures Graph does not expose Outlook signatures, so Zernio stores them. Create one and make it the default for an address: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/signatures" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "name": "Support", "html": "Contoso Support
support@contoso.com", "defaultFor": ["support@contoso.com"] }' ``` `appendSignature: true` then appends it to `html` and `text`, above the quoted original on replies. Pass `signatureId` to pick one explicitly. Without a default, `appendSignature` answers `400`. To switch the signature on a draft, `PATCH` it with the new `html` or `text` and `signatureId`. The old signature block is replaced, never stacked; `signatureId: null` removes it. ## Read and send from a shared mailbox A shared mailbox such as `support@contoso.com` can be added as an account of its own. Every endpoint on this page then takes its `accountId`. First connect the user's Microsoft account with the `shared_mailboxes` area. A connect without it never asks for the shared permissions, so other connections are unchanged: ```bash curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/connect/microsoft?profileId=PROFILE_ID&scopes=email,shared_mailboxes" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" ``` Then add the mailbox under that account: ```bash curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/shared-mailboxes" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "address": "support@contoso.com", "displayName": "Contoso Support" }' ``` The response carries the new `accountId`. `GET /v1/email/shared-mailboxes?accountId=…` lists the mailboxes added under an account. - **Access.** The user needs Full Access to the mailbox in Exchange, and Send As or Send on Behalf to send from it. Without Full Access the call answers `403` `shared_mailbox_access_denied`. A new grant can take up to an hour to reach Microsoft Graph. - **New mail.** Microsoft sends no change notifications for shared mailboxes opened this way. Zernio reads the Inbox every minute and fires `message.received` for each new email. - **Billing.** Each shared mailbox counts as a connected account. - **Removing.** `DELETE /v1/accounts/{accountId}` removes one. Disconnecting the user's account removes its shared mailboxes too. Gmail has no equivalent: a delegate cannot open another Gmail mailbox through Google's API. ## Categorize a message Outlook categories work as labels. Add or remove them by name with `addLabels` and `removeLabels`, and the message stays in its folder: ```bash curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/email/messages/MESSAGE_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "addLabels": ["Hermia/Handled"] }' ``` Each message lists its category names in `labels`. A name the mailbox has not used before is created on the message, so you do not need to create it first. `GET /v1/email/labels` lists the mailbox's categories, `POST /v1/email/labels` adds one and `DELETE /v1/email/labels/{labelId}` removes one by name. Deleting a category does not take it off messages that already carry it. ## Flag, move or trash `PATCH /v1/email/messages/{messageId}` and `PATCH /v1/email/threads/{threadId}` take `accountId` and any of `unread`, `starred` (Outlook's flag) and `folder`. Setting `folder` moves the mail, so `"folder": "archive"` archives it. `DELETE /v1/email/messages/{messageId}?accountId=…` moves a message to Deleted Items. ## Download an attachment Attachment ids come in each message's `attachments`. `GET /v1/email/attachments/{attachmentId}?accountId=…&messageId=…` streams the file with its `Content-Type` and filename. ## How it behaves - **Daily send cap.** 1,000 sends a day per mailbox, reset at midnight UTC. Every send answers with `X-Zernio-Send-Limit`, `X-Zernio-Send-Remaining` and `X-Zernio-Send-Reset`. `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/health` reports the same as `sendCap`. - **Bulk protection.** The same body sent to more than 50 distinct recipients within an hour pauses the mailbox: 10 minutes the first time, doubling up to 24 hours, and Zernio fires `account.rate_limited`. The mailbox is for one-to-one mail, not newsletters. - **Attachments.** 25 MB in total per email, the same as Gmail. Files over 3 MB are uploaded to Outlook in parts. Send large files by `url`, since a request body is capped at 4.5 MB. Attachments given by `url` must download within 20 seconds. - **Stable message ids.** A message keeps its `id` when it moves between folders, so ids from webhooks keep working after the user files the mail. Ids returned before 10 November 2026 changed on every move. They are still accepted everywhere, but the same message now comes back under its new, stable id. - **No payment gate.** Outlook sends do not need a payment method on the workspace. - **Inbox.** Mail received while the account is connected, and mail sent through the API, appears as [inbox](/messages/list-inbox-conversations) conversations, one per Outlook conversation, and fires `message.received` or `message.sent`. Older mail is reachable through these endpoints, not the inbox. - **Reads.** Reads are live calls to Microsoft Graph, are not metered, and count against your [API rate limit](/guides/rate-limits). When Graph throttles the mailbox, Zernio answers `429` `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. - **Folders.** If the provider does not answer, `GET /v1/email/folders` returns the last folder list read for that mailbox in the past 24 hours, with `"stale": true`, `"asOf"` and an `X-Zernio-Stale-As-Of` header, not a `502`. Unread and total counts may be out of date. Message lists are never served stale. ## If it fails | Error | Cause | Fix | |-------|-------|-----| | `429` `email_send_cap_reached` | The mailbox reached today's cap. `details.cap` has `limit`, `used` and `resetsAt` | Wait for `Retry-After` or `resetsAt`. | | `429` `rate_limited` | The mailbox is in a cooldown after a recipient burst, or Graph throttled it | Wait for `Retry-After`, and send fewer identical emails. | | `400` `invalid_field_value` | A field is invalid: a non `X-` header, attachments over 25 MB in total, `scheduledFor` outside 1 minute to 30 days, tracking without `html` | Fix the field named in `param`. | | `403` `from_not_allowed` | The mailbox has no Send As or Send on Behalf right on the `from` address | An Exchange admin grants the right, or send without `from`. | | `400` `from_not_allowed` | The address is neither listed nor declared | Declare it with `POST /v1/email/send-as`. | | `400` `signature_unavailable` | The sending address has no default Zernio signature | Create one with `defaultFor`, or pass `signatureId`. | | `412` `account_scope_missing` | The account has no `email` area | [Connect again](/platforms/microsoft/connect#add-areas-later) with `email` in `scopes`. | | `412` `admin_consent_required` | The organization requires an administrator's approval | Follow [admin consent](/platforms/microsoft/admin-consent). | | `401` `reconnect_required` | Microsoft refused the account's access | Reconnect the account. | | `409` `account_reconnect_required` | The account was disconnected after Microsoft refused its access. `details.reconnectPath` starts the sign-in again | Send the user through `details.reconnectPath`, or the `reconnectUrl` of `account.disconnected`. | | `403` `shared_mailbox_access_denied` | The user cannot open that shared mailbox | Grant the user Full Access in Exchange, then add it again. | | `412` `account_scope_missing` on a shared mailbox | The user's account lost the `shared_mailboxes` area | Reconnect it with `scopes=email,shared_mailboxes`. | ## Related - [List email threads](/email/list-email-threads) - [Send an email](/email/send-email-message) - [Reply to a message](/email/reply-email-message) - [List folders](/email/list-email-folders) - [List labels](/email/list-email-labels) - [List send-as addresses](/email/list-email-send-as) - [Declare a send-as address](/email/declare-email-send-as) - [Create a signature](/email/create-email-signature) - [Download an attachment](/email/download-email-attachment)
